title: Multiband reconstruction and crossover tests
description:
Add juce::UnitTest coverage for MultibandCrossover / MultibandEngine reconstruction and crossover behavior per SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §5.3 and §21.4.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/MultibandCrossover.*, MultibandZone.*, MultibandEngine.* public APIs
- tests/TestMain.cpp and existing tests/*Tests.cpp patterns (phases B–D)
- CMakeLists.txt as left by e.3 (tests/MultibandTests.cpp should already be listed — do not edit CMake unless the entry is missing, then append only that path)
- .abracapocus/SHREDEQ_SPEC.md §5.3 crossover defaults/ranges and §21.4 reconstruction requirements

Implement tests/MultibandTests.cpp:
1. Reconstruction: with all zone gains at unity and dynamics inactive/bypassed, broadband or multi-sine probe through MultibandEngine (or crossover split+sum) has flat magnitude vs dry within a documented tolerance (e.g. maxima of band FFT or multi-frequency tone magnitudes within ~±0.5 dB or tighter if stable) — NOT sample-identical (LR4 phase is frequency-dependent).
2. Enabling the engine at unity settings does not produce a large level jump versus bypass (RMS or peak within tolerance).
3. Crossover motion: sweeping crossover frequencies across a block/sequence yields finite output with no NaNs/Inf and no impulsive click artifacts beyond a stated peak transient bound versus a static-crossover control (energy or max-delta check).
4. Ordering protection: attempting to set crossovers out of order results in f1 < f2 < f3 effective frequencies.
5. Default crossover centers approximate 140 / 900 / 4500 Hz after prepare.
6. Solo/mute (if exposed): soloing one zone suppresses others in the sum; mute silences that zone.
7. reset() clears filter memory (finite output after impulse; no NaNs).

Use juce::UnitTest only; no Catch2/GoogleTest. Prefer public APIs; do not rewrite production DSP solely to force greens. Tolerance-based float compares with clear expect messages.

CMakeLists.txt is owned by e.3 — avoid editing unless the MultibandTests.cpp source entry is missing.
